To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of a dynamic dataflow architecture is determined by the average parallelism, scalability, and locality of the dataflow graphs that are executed in it.
The performance of a dynamic dataflow architecture is a function of the average parallelism, the granularity of parallelism and the degree of locality of the dataflow program.

(a) The scalability of the architecture is independent of the average parallelism, (b) The performance of a coarse grain parallel dataflow graph is better than that of a fine grain parallel one, and (c) The performance is better if the scheduling of the dataflow instructions is decentralized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the computation-communication issues that affect the performance of dynamic dataflow architectures.
the study of the performance of a dynamic dataflow architecture.
developing analytical models to study the performance of dynamic dataflow architectures, which are currently being developed for high performance computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamic dataflow architectures have the potential for achieving high performance in terms of speedup, throughput, and utilization.

a dynamic dataflow architecture can be designed to be scalable in the following sense: if the number of processors in the architecture is doubled, then the performance is doubled, and if the average parallelism in the dataflow graph is increased by a factor of two, the performance is increased by a similar factor.
the dynamic dataflow architectures are very promising for the execution of dataflow applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dynamic dataflow architecture with a large degree of decentralization in scheduling, and with fine grain parallelism is more scalable than an architecture without these features.
the dynamic dataflow architectures are scalable, but the performance of the architecture degrades as the degree of decentralization of dataflow scheduling and the locality of communication increases.
the performance of dynamic dataflow architectures is highly dependent on the degree of locality of communication and computation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the architecture is not affected by the degree of decentralization of scheduling.
the performance of a dynamic dataflow architecture is primarily determined by its average parallelism and not by its maximum parallelism.
dynamic dataflow architectures are scalable, but they are not as scalable as static dataflow architectures.
